To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Czech Republic is one of the most aid-intensive countries among EU members; 2) the Czech Republic’s industrial policy is not only very aid intensive but also highly selective; 3) the Czech Republic uses the EU state aid system to support its national champions and the state-owned companies; and 4) the Czech Republic does not use the EU state aid to support its SMEs.

(1) the state aid database of the European Commission (EC) is a useful source for research on industrial policy effects in the Czech Republic; (2) the state aid data is a useful complement to other data sources; (3) state aid data is not sufficient to study industrial policy effects in isolation; and (4) the state aid policy in the Czech Republic has had a limited positive effect on the Czech economy, but this effect has not been large enough to compensate for the negative effects
